central_concept: Multiple linear regression extends linear regression to several explanatory variables, fitting a regression plane and permitting nonlinear functions of explanatory variables while retaining linearity in parameters.
estimation_method: Method of least squares minimizes \(SS(b_0^*,\ldots,b_k^*)=\sum_{i=1}^n[y_i-(b_0^*+b_1^*x_{i1}+\cdots+b_k^*x_{ik})]^2\); normal equations are \(\mathbf X'\mathbf X\mathbf b=\mathbf X'\mathbf y\); unique solution \(\mathbf b=(\mathbf X'\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X'\mathbf y\) when explanatory variables are not linear combinations of one another.
data_representation: Data consist of \(k\) explanatory variables and one response for each of \(n\) observations: \((x_{i1},\ldots,x_{ik},y_i)\); \(\mathbf y\) is the \(n\times1\) response vector and \(\mathbf X\) is the \(n\times(k+1)\) explanatory-variable matrix.
model_assumptions: Observables representation F1--F5: linear conditional mean; nonstochastic \(x\)'s; \(\operatorname{Var}y_i=\sigma^2\); independent \(y_i\)'s; normally distributed \(y_i\)'s. Error representation E1--E5: additive errors; nonstochastic \(x\)'s; \(\textrm{E}\varepsilon_i=0\), \(\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon_i=\sigma^2\); independent and normal errors.
estimator_properties: Property 1: under F1--F4, \(\mathbf b\) is unbiased for \(\boldsymbol\beta\). Property 2: \(\operatorname{Var}\mathbf b=\sigma^2(\mathbf X'\mathbf X)^{-1}\). Gauss-Markov: least squares is minimum variance unbiased among estimators linear in responses. Property 3: under F1--F5, \(\mathbf b\) is normally distributed.
goodness_of_fit: Residuals are \(e_i=y_i-\widehat y_i\); \(s^2=\sum_{i=1}^ne_i^2/[n-(k+1)]\) is MSE and \(s\) is residual standard deviation. \(\text{Total SS}=\text{Error SS}+\text{Regression SS}\); \(R^2=\text{Regression SS}/\text{Total SS}\); \(R_a^2=1-[(\text{Error SS})/[n-(k+1)]]/[(\text{Total SS})/(n-1)]\).
inference_method: For \(H_0:\beta_j=d\), use \(t\text{-ratio}=(b_j-d)/se(b_j)\), where \(se(b_j)=s\sqrt{\text{the }(j+1)\text{st diagonal element of }(\mathbf X'\mathbf X)^{-1}}\). For a two-sided test reject when \(|t\text{-ratio}|>t_{n-(k+1),1-\alpha/2}\); confidence interval \(b_j\pm t_{n-(k+1),1-\alpha/2}se(b_j)\).
multivariate_diagnostic: Scatterplot and correlation matrices summarize only pairs of variables. Added variable plots control for other explanatory variables: regress \(y\) on all variables except \(x_j\), regress \(x_j\) on those same variables, then plot the first residuals against the second. Omitted variables can yield misleading coefficient significance or signs.
partial_correlation_relation: The partial correlation is the correlation between the two residual series in an added variable plot and measures the relationship between \(y\) and \(x_j\) in the presence of other explanatory variables. It can be calculated as \(t(b_j)/\sqrt{t(b_j)^2+n-(k+1)}\).
special_explanatory_variables: Binary variables are indicators or dummy variables, with coefficients interpreted as changes from the base category. Transformations include powers \(x,x^2,\ldots,x^p\), \(\ln x\), and categorized continuous variables. Interaction terms such as \(x_1x_2\) allow marginal effects to depend on other variables. Piecewise linear models use binary variables and interactions to represent kinks or discontinuities.
key_empirical_examples: Term Life Insurance: \(n=275\), LNFACE modeled using EDUCATION, NUMHH, and LNINCOME; fitted plane \(\widehat y=2.584+0.206x_1+0.306x_2+0.494x_3\). Female advantage: Lemaire's model of life-expectancy differences across 169 countries. Refrigerator Prices: \(n=37\), illustrating ECOST's positive marginal correlation but negative controlled coefficient. Life Insurance Company Expenses: Segal's output, quadratic, binary-interaction, and input-price model.
